contract: Publish shape contract (T-533). Declares, per functional directory of the ASSEMBLED publish tree, the minimum number of files that must appear DIRECTLY in that directory. Direct-child semantics only (dirOf(), non-recursive): a file in scripts/attic/ does NOT count towards scripts/. The empty-string key is the root pseudo-directory.
enforced_by: scripts/mavp-publish-overlay.js — loaded from the assembled tree in the read-only planning phase and enforced before any file is copied or deleted. Absent ledger = silent skip FOR THIS FLOOR CHECK ALONE — the separate succession gate below (T-541 round 3) may still print a loud stand-down line for the exact same absent-ledger case when the clone holds a previously published full anchor, so 'absent ledger' is never actually silent end to end unless the clone has nothing complete to compare against either. Present-but-malformed = hard refusal, where malformed includes an empty min_direct_files object, any floor below 1 (T-540), and any duplicate key within min_direct_files, regardless of whether its repeated values differ or are equal (T-541). A run that loads and passes prints one whole-line enforcement signal naming this path, the number of floors enforced, and a digest over every dir=floor pair so a compensating raise-and-lower cannot leave the signal byte-identical (T-541), so a release log distinguishes 'every floor enforced, unchanged' from 'the tier stood down' or 'a floor moved'. Separately (T-541 rounds 2-3), the overlay ALSO compares this file's own copy already sitting in the destination clone (the previously published ledger) against the one about to be published — see the top-level `succession_gate` field below for what that comparison covers, which this `enforced_by`/digest mechanism deliberately does not.
why_a_state_guard: Every other composition tier in the overlay is a per-RUN delta guard, and that whole family is composition-defeatable two ways: credited relocation is count-preserving, so the move-credit budget renews in full on every publish (four consecutive relocations of a quarter of the tree each pass, reaching the same drained end state as a single refused run), and the budgets have a denominator that unguarded ADDITIONS inflate (a padding publish lifts the baseline, so the next run's identical drain measures smaller). Floors on the assembled END STATE are immune to both by construction: four runs of 47 relocations and one run of 147 hit the same check on the same end state, and an absolute floor never reads the baseline at all, so padding changes nothing.
how_to_relax: There is no runtime override and no flag: --allow-mass-delete does NOT suppress a contract refusal. The single sanctioned relaxation is editing this committed file, which IS the operator-review moment this tier exists to create — a reviewable diff on a small, human-readable ledger. Deleting the file (or dropping it from the manifest's ship bucket) stands the tier down entirely; that is accepted, at the same trust level as editing scripts/publish-manifest.json itself, and it is equally a reviewable diff. Lowering a floor while leaving `derivation.observed_direct_file_counts_at_seeding` and `derivation.seeded_on` untouched is the SANCTIONED relaxation and is never refused by the succession gate (T-541 round 2, see `succession_gate` below) — it only prints a non-blocking weakening line naming the directory and both values, so the review trail is loud without being a runtime override. Re-seeding the observed counts themselves (rather than just a floor) is a DIFFERENT, more consequential edit and must satisfy the three succession-gate rules named there — it is not covered by this simpler floor-only path. T-545 CLOSES the CI-side half of this floor-only path: an OPTIONAL top-level `floor_relaxations` field (top level DELIBERATELY, never inside `derivation` — see `succession_gate` for why) maps a directory key to `{floor, on, why}` and, in the SAME edit that lowers a floor here, declares that exact directory, the new strictly-lower committed floor, a canonical YYYY-MM-DD date and a non-empty reason; Test 41 (scripts/test-publish-overlay.js) folds every declared entry's floor value over its own recomputed result before comparing against the committed floor map, so a declared lowering passes Test 41 while a silent (undeclared) one still reddens it. The declared floor must sit STRICTLY below floor_rule's recomputed value for that directory — a stale or raise-shaped entry (a later re-seed dropped the recomputed floor to or below the declared value) reddens Test 41 naming the one-line fix: delete the entry. Declaring a relaxation is purely a CI and review artifact — it changes nothing about what is enforced at publish time, which remains owned entirely by the weakening line above, and the succession gate deliberately never reads this field (see `succession_gate`).
succession_gate: T-541 rounds 2-4. Round 1's recompute invariant (Test 41, scripts/test-publish-overlay.js) reads BOTH `derivation.observed_direct_file_counts_at_seeding` and `min_direct_files` from THIS SAME file, so a coherent one-shot edit of both together (e.g. observed 9 -> 3, floor 5 -> floor_rule(3, 0.6) = 2 on one directory) passes Test 41 by construction — reproduced end to end, draining a directory three files below its true committed floor at exit 0. Test 41 is now honestly scoped as a DRIFT invariant against a sloppy re-seed (arithmetic mistake, stale fraction, a forgotten key), not a forgery check (see Test 41's own comment in scripts/test-publish-overlay.js for that scope statement, unchanged since round 2) — it cannot be, since a forger has every input Test 41 has. The forgery class is instead owned by scripts/mavp-publish-overlay.js's checkShapeContractSuccession(), which compares this file's copy ALREADY PUBLISHED in the destination clone (a one-step history no same-commit forgery can rewrite — the mirror is the memory) against the one about to be published. GUARANTEE, stated as its THREE ACCEPTED STATES (round 3): whenever the clone holds a full previously-published anchor (observed counts + seeded_on + floors), the decision is TOTAL over the assembled side — exactly three states are accepted, everything else refuses before any write: (1) the seeding record byte-identical to what the clone last published -> SILENT (ordinary growth stays green); (2) a valid, DATED, delta-verified RE-SEED -> LOUD (a re-seed line, plus any weakening/removed-key lines); (3) the ledger deleted from the assembled tree entirely -> LOUD STAND-DOWN (the sanctioned relaxation in how_to_relax above, made visible rather than silent). Round 2 shipped the anchor but left the activation condition lenient — it returned dormant whenever the assembled ledger's derivation was absent or partial, which let the round-1 forgery plus a deleted `seeded_on` publish silently at exit 0 against a full clone anchor; round 3 closes that (absent-or-partial assembled derivation against a full clone anchor now REFUSES, naming these three green paths). On any publish where the seeding record itself changed — EITHER `observed_direct_file_counts_at_seeding` OR a bare `derivation.seeded_on` rewrite differing from the clone's previously published value (round 3; round 2 compared only the observed maps, so a bare bump, forward or backdated, was silently dormant) — three rules must ALL hold or the publish is refused before any write: (1) DATED — `seeded_on` must strictly advance past the previously published date; a record that changed without its date advancing is a falsified historical observation. Canonical YYYY-MM-DD format is validated on the about-to-be-published date whenever this rule is evaluated (never on a dormant publish). Round 3 let a non-canonical PUBLISHED date (pre-round-3 history this file's own past could not be edited to fix) skip only the strict-advance comparison, loudly, rather than refuse on its shape — round 4 DELETES that leniency outright: a non-canonical PUBLISHED seeded_on now REFUSES, naming the self-serve two-publish repair (stand down by deleting this file, then re-introduce it) that needs no mirror surgery. This is safe because round 4 also closes off every path that could CREATE a non-canonical published anchor going forward — see COHERENT and RECORD INTRODUCTION below — so the leniency was protecting only pre-round-4 history, and this repo's own published seeded_on is already canonical. (2) REAL — every re-seeded observed count must equal the assembled tree's own actual direct file count AT THIS PUBLISH; this is the one moment recorded and live must coincide by definition, which is exactly why the gate stays dormant (and growth stays green) on every publish where the record is untouched, unlike a strict recorded-equals-live rule checked on every run. (3) REACHABLE — every re-seeded observed count must be >= the PREVIOUSLY PUBLISHED FLOOR for that directory (not the previously published observed count): legitimate shrinkage toward a floor, followed by an honest re-seed AT that floor, must still pass. DELTA SCOPE (round 3): rules 2 and 3 examine ONLY the directories whose recorded observed count actually differs between the previously published and the about-to-be-published record — never every recorded key. Iterating every key blamed directories nobody touched: a sanctioned partial re-seed of one directory was refused citing an untouched directory whose recorded count had simply drifted from ordinary repo growth (measured live: re-seeding docs/assets alone, refused citing scripts recorded below its already-grown live count). A brand-new key gets REAL but not REACHABLE (no previously published floor to reach for a key that did not exist before — see residual (a) below). A key dropped from the record entirely prints a loud, non-refusing line rather than participating in either rule. None of this reopens the ordinary end-state floor check: a stale recorded count is never a defence against an actual live-tree drain, since findShapeContractViolations() reads live counts, never recorded ones, on every publish regardless of this gate's own state. Separately, on every publish where BOTH sides carry a full anchor (record changed or not): a floor that moved down or was dropped relative to the previously published ledger prints a loud, NON-refusing weakening line naming the directory and both values — this must never be a refusal, since how_to_relax above names floor-only lowering as the sanctioned relaxation. GUARANTEE ACTUALLY DELIVERED: per-step MONOTONICITY plus MANDATORY VISIBILITY, never 'forgery is impossible'. ROUND 4 closes two more findings, both keyed on ATTACKER-EDITABLE input, both reproduced end to end at exit 0 on the real CLI, both closed structurally. FINDING 1 — the delta partition above has THREE parts (changed, added, removed) and rounds 2-3 covered only two: a key DELETED from `observed_direct_file_counts_at_seeding` (rather than edited) lands in the removed bucket, is examined by neither REAL nor REACHABLE, and the re-seed line used to print prose claiming every re-seeded count was verified — about a directory neither rule had touched. COHERENT closes this structurally rather than teaching REAL/REACHABLE one more case: whenever the assembled derivation is full, every key declared in `min_direct_files` must have a matching key in `observed_direct_file_counts_at_seeding`, checked FIRST and UNCONDITIONALLY (independent of the clone's own anchor state, since this is a same-commit invariant on the assembled ledger alone) — a floor with no matching observation is an enforcement value whose provenance was deleted, and it refuses regardless of which delta bucket the missing key would otherwise have landed in. Retiring a directory WHOLLY (both its floor and its observation, together) still passes loudly via the pre-existing removal and weakening lines, since neither side declares the key at all. The real committed ledger satisfies COHERENT today: 18 declared floor keys against 18 declared observed keys. FINDING 2 — the record-introduction path never validated the incoming `seeded_on`, so a manufactured non-canonical value became the clone's new anchor and was then treated as lenient legacy history on every later publish (repeatable via stand-down -> genesis -> re-introduce, since genesis was unconditionally silent and stand-down is non-refusing). RECORD INTRODUCTION is now validated: GENESIS (no clone ledger at all) and the pre-existing partial-anchor case are unified into one event, format- and COHERENT-checked before printing its loud INTRODUCED line — genesis is no longer silent. ROUND 4 CORRECTED: introduction does NOT apply REAL — its observed counts are recorded AS CLAIMED, NOT verified against the live tree (trust-on-first-use), because REAL's semantics ('this recorded count was observed AT THIS PUBLISH') is true only for the changed/added delta of a DATED re-seed, where the operator attests a fresh observation; comparing a HISTORICAL introduced record against the CURRENT live tree is a category error that refused the single most common introduction case there is (an honest mirror catching up to a canonical side that kept growing since the record was seeded), and it bound no adversary either, since a same-commit forger simply sets observed equal to their own evacuated tree's live counts. Introduction deliberately also does NOT apply REACHABLE (the sanctioned lower-then-reseed protocol legitimately collapses into one introduction publish when no record existed before; the weakening line carries the visibility) — a documented residual, adjacent to T-545. T-549 (a MEDIUM residual out of the round-4 security review): the INTRODUCED line now additionally prints, per introduced observed key, the claimed count beside the assembled tree's own live direct count (buildDirectCountMap()), labeled informational and NOT verified — this closes a DIFFERENTIAL, not the trust-on-first-use hole itself (verification-at-introduction remains a deliberate non-decision: TOFU is inherent to the first anchor, and any introduction-time CHECK is satisfiable by a same-commit forger by construction). Before T-549 a STAND-DOWN then a fabricated RECORD-INTRODUCTION was cheaper than the disclosed N-step loud ratchet (residual (b) below) only because neither of its two loud lines carried a number a reviewer could act on; printing claimed-vs-live degrades the swap back into the ratchet, since a fabricated claimed=1 beside a live tree of 500 now indicts itself in the same line, while an honest mirror catch-up (claimed 108, live 114) still prints without being refused. The decision function is unchanged by this: no accept/refuse branch reads the live map, which is computed only on this introduction path, never on a dormant publish. THE DURABLE INVARIANT: a refusal may compare a recorded value to the live tree only where the record itself asserts observation-at-this-publish — round 3's original all-keys Rule 2 and round 4's (corrected) introduction REAL were the identical defect, in different branches, with the same two numbers (a recorded 108 against a live 114). ADDED keys additionally gain REACHABLE, but only when the clone's previously published floor map already declares a floor for that exact (brand-new-to-the-observed-record) key: dead code against any anchor the gate itself has admitted since round 4 shipped (COHERENT there guarantees a floored key always has a matching observed key), live only against a LEGACY pre-round-4 anchor that itself already violates COHERENT. Finally, the re-seed CERTIFICATE is now GENERATED rather than narrated: it reports the changed-key count and names (REAL+REACHABLE-verified), the added-key count and names (REAL-verified), and the removed-key count and names (each with the floor it stood down with) directly from the arrays the rules iterated, so it can never claim verification of a directory the code did not check — exactly finding 1's defect class. INDUCTIVE INVARIANT, why deleting the DATED leniency (rule 1 above) is safe: the only write paths through this gate from here on are introduction, byte-identical, re-seed and stand-down, and introduction always format- and COHERENT-validates — so every full anchor the gate itself ever admits from here on is canonical-dated and coherent, PLUS entry-verified against the live tree for any key a subsequent re-seed actually touches (an introduction-created anchor's observed values stay trust-on-first-use until then, by design). HONEST TRUST MODEL, stated plainly rather than implied: this gate is a procedural TRIPWIRE that raises the cost of the cheapest SILENT edit — it is not a cryptographic guarantee. A commit-level adversary can edit the gate's own code (scripts/mavp-publish-overlay.js) in the same commit as any forgery; the pre-push human review of that diff is the actual backstop this gate assists, not replaces. NOT PROTECTED, said plainly: a reviewer rubber-stamping every step of an N-step loud ratchet; floor VALUES chosen at genesis or introduction (COHERENT checks presence of a matching observed key, never that the chosen floor or observed value is itself honest); remove-then-readd (now costing two loud publishes instead of one, per finding 1's fix, but still not blocked); and clone-mirror provenance beyond parse-refusal (an unparseable mirror refuses, but a mirror that parses cleanly and was tampered with consistently is trusted as-is). RESIDUALS, deliberately not closed by this gate, all closed by diff review at the same trust level as deleting this ledger outright: (a) GENESIS and RECORD-INTRODUCTION not applying REACHABLE (see ROUND 4 above — this is now the only remaining piece of the original residual (a); the silence itself is closed); (b) an N-step LOUD RATCHET — re-seed 9 -> 5 (weakening line), drain, re-seed 5 -> 3 (weakening line), drain, and so on; each step is dated and its own reviewable diff plus a printed weakening event, but nothing stops a reviewer rubber-stamping every step in sequence; (c) REMOVE-THEN-READD — dropping a declared key prints a loud removal line, but re-declaring that same directory afresh at the drained count is then a brand-new key with no previously published floor to compare against (round 4: unless the clone's own LEGACY anchor already declares a floor for that exact key with no matching observed entry, in which case REACHABLE still applies — dead code against any anchor the gate itself has admitted since round 4 shipped); (d) out-of-band tampering with the clone MIRROR itself — an unparseable or corrupted previously-published copy there refuses, naming the mirror as the thing to investigate, regardless of the assembled side's own state, but the gate has no way to verify the mirror's own provenance beyond that. T-545 CLOSES the separate question of a sanctioned floor-only lowering passing Test 41's own equality invariant without touching this seeding record at all, via the optional top-level `floor_relaxations` field (see `how_to_relax` and `derivation.maintenance` for the full protocol). THIS GATE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT READ `floor_relaxations`, and that omission is load-bearing, not an oversight: declaration is a CI and review artifact, publish-time visibility of a floor lowering is already owned end to end by the non-refusing weakening line above (it fires on every full-anchor publish regardless of whether a lowering was declared), and a gate branch keyed on this attacker-editable field would be exactly the twice-produced defect shape — a lenient branch keyed on attacker-editable input — that FINDING 1 and FINDING 2 above (and round 3's original DATED leniency) each closed structurally rather than by adding one more special case. `floor_relaxations` living at the top level rather than inside `derivation` is what makes this provable rather than asserted: `recordChanged` above compares only `observed_direct_file_counts_at_seeding` and `seeded_on`, both scoped to `derivation`, so a declared relaxation can never flip `recordChanged` and the succession gate stays DORMANT on this path exactly as it already was before this field existed.

derivation.seeded_from: the real ship set as produced by scripts/mavp-publish-assemble.js — every directory that held at least one file directly, counted non-recursively
derivation.rounding: floor(observed x fraction) is only the FIRST of three terms — see floor_rule for the complete expression, which is what any re-seed must apply. Every floor is finally clamped up to a minimum of 1.
derivation.floor_rule: floor(dir) = max( floor(observed(dir) x fraction), observed(dir) <= 4 ? observed(dir) - 1 : 0, isLocationSemantic(dir) ? observed(dir) : 0 ), clamped up to a minimum of 1. This COMPLETE expression, not the base fraction alone, is the seeding algorithm. Re-seeding from a then-current ship set with the flat fraction would silently regress the three floors T-540 raised (the top-level .claude bucket, .claude/rules, .claude/agents) back to values the pre-existing full-wipe rule already covered — a no-op tier for exactly the directories that hold this project's own enforcement machinery. The armed re-seeding recheck must reproduce all three terms; that is why the algorithm is codified here and not just its output.
derivation.floor_rule_term_1_base_fraction: floor(observed x fraction), fraction = 0.6 — the volume term, justified in why_0_6_and_not_0_5 below. It governs every bucket of 5 or more files that is not location-semantic, i.e. every large directory here.
derivation.floor_rule_term_2_small_directory: observed <= 4 ? observed - 1 : 0 — the small-directory term (T-540, T-533 security review residual 2). The base fraction COLLAPSES on small buckets: floor(3 x 0.6) = 1 leaves a 3-file directory free to lose 2 of its 3 files, so its effective retention is 33 percent, and the line the ledger actually drew there was 'not empty' — a line the overlay's pre-existing full-wipe rule already drew for free. So the fraction contributed nothing for small buckets, while the ledger claimed that declaring every directory covered the small-directory class. It did not. This term makes the floor bind at ONE file of shrinkage for buckets of 2 to 4 files, which is the tightest rule that still lets a small directory shrink at all.
derivation.floor_rule_term_3_location_semantic: isLocationSemantic(dir) ? observed : 0 — the location-semantic term: floor equals observed, i.e. no shrinkage at all without an edit here. isLocationSemantic() is the overlay's OWN predicate (LOCATION_SEMANTIC_PREFIXES), deliberately reused rather than re-listed in this ledger so the two tiers can never drift apart; applied to a directory key it is evaluated as that directory's own child prefix. These are the paths whose files derive their function from their LOCATION rather than their bytes — CI workflows, the commit hook, the rules files, the agent specs — so losing one is never routine evolution, it is a change to what enforces the project. The reviewer's reproduction that motivated this term removed 9 such files (2 of 3 rules files, 5 of 11 agent specs, 2 of 3 top-level .claude files) in one publish at exit 0 with no output.
derivation.floor_rule_combination: The three terms are independent lower bounds and the STRONGEST one wins (max), then the clamp to at least 1 applies. A floor of 0 is a no-op entry — satisfied by an empty directory — and the loader now REFUSES one rather than accepting it (see enforced_by). Against the observed counts recorded below, exactly three floors are decided by a term other than the base fraction: the top-level .claude bucket (observed 3, small-directory term, floor 2), .claude/rules (observed 3, location-semantic term, floor 3) and .claude/agents (observed 11, location-semantic term, floor 11). Two further single-file buckets (.claude/hooks, .github/workflows) are decided identically by the location-semantic term and the clamp, and every remaining floor is the base fraction unchanged.
derivation.legitimate_release_cost: Priced deliberately, not left implicit. (a) A small NON-enforcement directory may still shrink by one file and passes at EQUALITY, because a floor is a minimum, not a trip-line — the frontend-design skill bucket (observed 2, floor 1) is the worked example. (b) Removing ANY file from a location-semantic enforcement directory now requires the one-line edit here, because those floors equal their observed counts. That cost IS the intent: retiring an agent spec or a rules file is precisely the change that must not ride along inside a publish unreviewed, and the edit is the operator-review moment this tier exists to create. (c) .claude/agents sits at count == floor == 11, so the equality boundary is exercised by the real ship set on every release; ADDING files never needs an edit, since floors are minimums.
derivation.why_0_6_and_not_0_5: 0.5 is provably too loose to be the fraction here, and that is not a judgment call: the reproduction this tier must subsume deletes 51 of a 104-file scripts/ bucket in one run (49.0% — under every per-run ratio tier) leaving 53 files, and 0.5 of the observed count would put the floor at or below 53, which passes at equality since a floor is a minimum, not a trip-line. The fraction therefore has to sit strictly above one half for the largest bucket; 0.6 is the next round number, and it leaves every directory ~40% of headroom for ordinary release evolution — far more than any release in this project's history has removed from a single directory in one publish. Erring tight is cheap here: a false trip costs one reviewable ledger edit and stands no other tier down, unlike an operator reaching for --allow-mass-delete.
derivation.why_no_exemption_for_small_directories: The per-run tiers exempt buckets below a size floor because ratio math on 1-4 files is noise. An absolute floor has no such problem, and the earlier security review found that hand-curated small-directory exemptions are exactly where the surviving attacks lived (the project's own enforcement machinery — hooks, rules, workflows, skills — is all single-digit directories). So every directory in the ship set at seeding time is declared, with no exemptions; a floor of 0 would be a no-op entry, hence the clamp to 1. Declaring them was necessary but NOT sufficient: with the base fraction alone their floors landed at 1, i.e. 'not empty', which the pre-existing full-wipe rule already guaranteed — see floor_rule_term_2_small_directory and floor_rule_term_3_location_semantic for the two terms that make the declaration bite.
derivation.scope_note: Floors describe the ASSEMBLED tree, so a directory that exists only in the public mirror (a `preserve` bucket path, e.g. issue templates) must never be declared here — it is never part of the assembled tree and would fail on every publish. Checking the assembled tree alone is also the conservative choice: the clone's end state is the assembled tree PLUS preserved paths, and preserved paths are additive, so they can only raise a directory's real count, never lower it.
derivation.residual: A floor counts files, not function: padding a declared directory with junk files satisfies its floor. That residual is not closed here — it is closed upstream, by the assembler being an allow-list over the git index (a padding file must be committed AND manifest-classified) and by the content-provenance gate that verifies assembled bytes against HEAD blobs.
derivation.maintenance: Adding a directory needs no edit (undeclared directories are not checked). Removing a directory, or shrinking one below its floor, requires an edit here — deliberately. Re-seeding after significant growth is optional; the floors are minimums, not targets, and a PARTIAL re-seed (only the directories that actually need refreshing) is fully sanctioned — the succession gate's delta scope (T-541 round 3, see `succession_gate`) means an untouched directory's stale recorded count is never examined or blamed. Any directory you DO re-seed MUST apply floor_rule in full (all three terms plus the clamp) against the then-current ship set and must record its new observed count alongside it — applying the base fraction alone is a silent regression, not a re-seed. A re-seed edit is also enforced at PUBLISH time by the succession gate (see the top-level `succession_gate` field), which checks the same commit against the previously published copy already sitting in the destination clone. The re-seed protocol this edit must satisfy is exactly the gate's three rules, applied only to the directories you touched: (1) DATED — bump `derivation.seeded_on` to a date strictly after the currently published one (in canonical YYYY-MM-DD form — a bare bump with every observed count otherwise unchanged is itself a valid, loud, empty-delta re-seed); (2) REAL — set every re-seeded `observed_direct_file_counts_at_seeding[dir]` to that directory's actual direct file count in the ship set AT THE PUBLISH where the re-seed lands (not at edit time — if the tree drifts between the ledger edit and the publish, re-seed again from the tree as it then stands); (3) REACHABLE — never re-seed an observed count below the CURRENTLY PUBLISHED floor for that directory (shrinking toward a floor and then re-seeding AT that floor is fine; re-seeding below it is not — lower the floor explicitly first, which is a separate, loud, non-refused edit). Then re-run floor_rule as usual over every re-seeded directory's new observed count to produce its new floor. Deleting this file entirely is the sanctioned full stand-down (how_to_relax above) and now always prints a loud line when the clone holds a full anchor, never silent as it was pre-round-3. T-545 — a FLOOR-ONLY lowering (as distinct from the re-seed protocol above, which also touches `observed_direct_file_counts_at_seeding`) is declared via the optional top-level `floor_relaxations` field: in the SAME edit that lowers a floor in `min_direct_files`, add `floor_relaxations[dir] = {floor: <the new, strictly lower, committed floor>, on: <canonical YYYY-MM-DD>, why: <non-empty reason>}`. The declared `floor` must sit STRICTLY below `floor_rule`'s recomputed value for that directory (recomputed from the UNCHANGED, still-recorded `observed_direct_file_counts_at_seeding`) or Test 41 reddens naming the violation. Remove the entry once a later re-seed drops the recomputed floor to or below it — Test 41 catches a stale entry the same way and names the one-line fix: delete the entry. This field is CI/review-only and is never read by checkShapeContractSuccession() (see `succession_gate`).
